terra.problem: “Whatever this beast has” goes beyond the power, throne and authority the text says the dragon gave it.
It guesses why Michael’s name came to the baker’s mind, which Papa Dorin has not been told.
The text says the wound was healed, not that it went away.
It states that the healing is what gets everyone’s attention. The verse reports the healing and the world’s reaction but does not explicitly give that reason.
It says the healing makes the world marvel. The verse reports both events but does not explicitly state that cause.
The text does not say the people watched the wound being healed.
It assumes the number felt right to the baker and claims to know why.
“The beast doesn’t turn on him” goes beyond the text, which says whom the beast blasphemes.
“The voice is a dragon’s” drops the comparison. The text says the beast spoke like a dragon.
The healing was not in the last verse; the preceding verse describes fire coming down. The passage also does not say the second beast never heals people.
It says the people did not get fair notice, though the passage does not address that.
Being permitted to give breath does not establish that the beast lacked power of its own to do so.
